title: Intrauterine insemination (IUI)
what: Prepared sperm is placed in the womb with a thin, soft tube on your ovulation days. This brings the sperm closer to the egg.
why: For sperm quality problems, cervical issues, unexplained infertility, or when using donor sperm.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; a pregnancy test about 2 weeks later
tell_doctor: If your fallopian tubes are open. This is checked beforehand
What medicines and hormones you take

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Both partners have tests beforehand, including a tube check and a semen analysis.

prepare.title: Ovulation
prepare.text: Ovulation is tracked by ultrasound, sometimes helped with medicine or a trigger shot. Your doctor will set the time.

prepare.title: Partner
prepare.text: Your partner gives a sperm sample on the day. Usually 2 to 5 days without ejaculation beforehand. Check with the clinic.

steps: Your partner's or donor sperm is prepared in the lab. This takes 1 to 2 hours
You lie in the gynecological chair
A thin, soft tube is passed through the cervix into the womb, and the sperm is slowly released
You lie still for a little while, then you can go
feel: Usually like a smear test, a little unpleasant
Sometimes mild cramps low in the belly
after: You can go about your normal life, without heavy exertion
Sometimes hormone support is prescribed. Take it as scheduled
A pregnancy test or blood test about 2 weeks later
red_flags: Severe belly pain, bloating, or shortness of breath after ovarian stimulation: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: How many tries are usually needed?
faq.a: Often up to 3 to 4 cycles are tried. If it does not work, your doctor will suggest other options.

faq.q: Do I need to lie down for long afterward?
faq.a: No. Usually 10 to 15 minutes is enough.

reminders.text: Insemination tomorrow. Your partner gives the sample at the set time. Bring both partners' documents.
